note: [agent-bulk] shw 3007 (100.0 MeV, 4 seg, cluster 3): correct. Yellow member set covers the whole visible cone from the X out to the far end on all three vertex cameras (az-055/az+065 el+20, az-055 el+60); one apex, no kink, no second direction, and no straight MIP stem swallowed. Nothing contiguous is left grey inside the cone: the only three non-members in the event are 28009 (pdg 13, 3.0 cm, 22.3 cm away at 96.4 deg to the axis), 29010 (pdg 11, 0.06 cm, 5.4 cm at 120.0 deg) and 84011 (pdg 2212, 0.7 cm, 4.5 cm at 171.8 deg) -- all sideways or behind the shower start, i.e. there is nothing in this event to add. Vertex judged first and cleared: the blue star carries the 84011 proton stub and sits on the backward extension of 3007's axis (171.8 deg), and the shower start is 4.9 cm out along that axis, which reads as a conversion gap rather than a misplaced vertex. Uncovered point cloud at the shower front is the spreading EM front, not an unclaimed segment, so it is not counted as under-clustering. Scope: 2 of 3 showers in scope (min kine_best 20 MeV); shower 29010 skipped at 1.1 MeV and not examined. No pi0: this event has no reco pi0 group and only one EM object above 20 MeV, so there is no second gamma to pair -- the same 'no partner in the reconstruction' case as pilot evt284200. Statement is about clustering only, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] Verdict is on the leading EM shower 22006 (259.1 MeV, 3 seg, cluster 22): correct. It is detached 25.1 cm from the vertex, its three members span 0-16.4 cm at 0-4.2 deg, and on both shower azimuths (az-055, az+085) the yellow set runs the full length of the blue cloud from the X back-pointing at the vertex to the far end, one apex, no kink. Every non-member is >=59 deg off its axis (nearest in angle is 48021 at 59.1 deg), so there is nothing contiguous and on-axis to add. Vertex judged first and cleared: on all three vertex cameras the 86.5 cm muon 19031 (correctly left unowned, grey), the apex of shower 49028 (3.5 cm) and the 12.8 cm segment 19032 all converge on the blue star. OVER-CLUSTERING ON A DIFFERENT SHOWER, and it is the finding of this event: shower 19032 (81.3 MeV, 2 seg) owns 40008, a 0.66 cm pdg 2212 stub 113.6 cm away, absorbed by pass3_cone at 20.0 deg tier 2. On shw19032-az-055-el+20 its yellow halo is in two disconnected places -- a 12.8 cm stub on the vertex, and a single point sitting on the far END of the muon track 113 cm away, with nothing of 19032 in between. Marked OUT. Second, smaller: shower 49028 (128.6 MeV, apex on the vertex) owns 46019, a 1.31 cm pdg 2212 stub at 42.6 cm / 23.7 deg absorbed by pass4_angle, which on shw49028-az-055-el+20 is visibly detached from the shower body (same shape as pilot evt400504's 21003). Marked OUT; charge is negligible, it is a PID/association statement not a geometry one. Note also that 19032 shares cluster 19 with the muon and reads dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against it -- possibly a vertex/muon-stem blob rather than an EM shower, but I did not test that and make no PID claim. Scope: 4 of 6 showers in scope (22006, 49028, 19032, 50029); 47020 (5.1 MeV) and 48021 (1.1 MeV) skipped by the 20 MeV rule and not examined. Pi0: no reco pi0 group. The capture's automatic slot assignment priced 22006+49028 at 221.9 MeV (axis) / 58.5 MeV (vertex), but 49028's apex is 3.5 cm from the star, i.e. vertex-attached, so it cannot be a converted photon and that pairing should not be read as a pi0 -- 22006 is the only detached photon-like object in the event and it has no plausible partner (50029 is 20.4 MeV at 62 deg to it). No pi0 candidate stored.

[agent-bulk] Verdict on the leading EM shower 7040 (949.6 MeV, 16 seg): leans correct, but I could not settle it, hence unclear. Reading (a) correct: all 16 members lie within 11.2 deg of one axis, one apex at the vertex, the body is continuous 0-55 cm and the rest is the tail of a 950 MeV shower (55 cm is only ~4 X0). Reading (b) over-clustered: the member set has a 21.7 cm gap (76.3 -> 98.0 cm) and then six more stub segments out to 120 cm (88168/88169/44061/87159/49066/87163, 14.2 cm of segment length, all pass3_cone tier 2) that on shw7040-az-055 and az+085 are visibly detached blobs, not part of a continuous body. The images do not separate the two readings and the acceptance plot does not either. HARNESS LIMITATION on this event: the vertex sweep is unusable -- r95 is 424 cm because of a 483 cm through-going muon, so the six vtx-* frames were rendered at +-400 cm and resolve nothing near the star. Every judgement here rests on the shower-framed captures (7040 at +-73 cm, 79136 +-47, 75099 +-62, 72076 +-30). Vertex nevertheless reads sane in those frames: the 483 cm muon 7172 and the 71.6 cm pion 7039 (both correctly left unowned) both start on the star, and 7040/75099/79136/72076 fan out from it. OBSERVATION worth the owner's eye, measured not inferred: six segments -- 72173, 72083, 72084, 72086, 72087, 72082, about 37 cm of cluster-72 skeleton -- are members of BOTH shower 79136 (625.6 MeV, where they sit at 27-29 deg, no tier, added by from_vertices walk_add) AND shower 72076 (127.3 MeV, where they sit at 1.5-9.2 deg, tier 1). Their charge is therefore inside both energy figures. I do not know whether overlapping membership is by design in this reconstruction, so I make no verdict on it. Note the display's own 'in shower' column is first-owner-wins (owner_map), so it shows only 79136 for those six; the per-shower count in cmp_div is what reveals the overlap. Smaller item: 71074 (2.7 cm pdg 13 at 19.4 cm / 5.2 deg, tier 1) is a non-member sitting inside 72076's pass-1 acceptance box -- a small under-clustering of 72076, not marked. No marks recorded on this event. Scope: 4 of 14 showers in scope (7040 949.6, 79136 625.6, 75099 301.2, 72076 127.3 MeV); the other 10 (40057 4.9, 27044 4.7, 37054 3.5, 51068 2.5, 47064 2.5, 24041 2.0, 32049 1.7, 43060 1.2, 50067 0.6, 48065 0.6 MeV) are all under 5 MeV, were skipped by the 20 MeV rule, and I did not look at them. Pi0: no reco pi0 group. The capture's automatic slots priced 7040+79136 at 460.6 MeV (axis convention; the vertex convention returns no chord because 7040 starts on the vertex), and the kine_pio_ BDT feature says 453.9 MeV and does not close with its own formula (525.2). Both members of that pair are vertex-attached or near it (7040 at 0.0 cm, 79136 at 18.0 cm), so neither reads as a converted photon and I propose no pi0 pairing.

[agent-bulk] Shower 79023 (295.0 MeV, 11 seg) is over-clustered, and its axis is pointing backwards. THE NUMBER THAT SAYS IT: its own cmp_div reads 'already in shower 79023 : 11 segment(s) -- distance 0.0-85.9 cm, angle 0.0-150.3 deg'. Ten of its eleven members sit at 128-150 deg to its own axis. Its acceptance plot has exactly ONE orange square in the whole pass-1 gate box -- the seed at (0.3 cm, 0.2 deg); every other member is off the top of the plot, brought in by from_vertices (walk_add) and pass4_angle, not by the cone. WHAT THE PICTURE SHOWS: the event is a vertex with a 7.7 cm stem and three detached blobs. On vtx-az-055 and vtx-az+065 the stem (segment 79023, site stem_backfill) leaves the star on the OPPOSITE side from every blob, and the orange axis arrow on shw79023-az-055 points away from the shower's entire body. The blobs are (i) 80055's compact shower at 26.7-43.0 cm, (ii) the cluster-19 group at 27.9-51.9 cm, (iii) the 82063 group at 67.6-86.4 cm. Measured 3-D separations: stem to cluster-19 27.9 cm, cluster-19 to 82063 24.1 cm, stem to 80055 24.7 cm -- three real gaps, not projection. Shower 79023 merges (i-not) the stem + group (ii) + group (iii), i.e. three apexes and ~150 deg of direction spread in one shower. MARKS: the seed stem 79023 marked OUT (it is on the far side of the vertex from the whole body, 131-146 deg from every member, and it is what sets the reversed axis); the far group 82063 + 81062 + 69018 + 67016 marked OUT (a separate narrow 20.6 cm streak behind a 24.1 cm gap). What should survive as the shower is the cluster-19 group. Shower 80055 (198.9 MeV) by contrast looks correct: 10 members over 0-49.3 cm within 22.7 deg, compact and contiguous, start on the vertex side of its blob, detached 26.7 cm from the star -- photon-like and I found nothing to add or remove. Vertex judged first and NOT called bad: only a 7.7 cm stub touches the star, but all three blobs sit 26-30 cm from it in different directions, which is what a common origin looks like; I would rather report the shower defect than blame the vertex. Scope: 2 of 9 showers in scope (79023, 80055); the other seven (68017 2.6, 30010 2.5, 64013 1.5, 71020 1.4, 63012 1.0, 65014 0.7, 62011 0.4 MeV) are all under 3 MeV, skipped by the 20 MeV rule, not examined. Pi0: no reco pi0 group. The capture's automatic slots priced 79023+80055 at 407.0 MeV on the axis convention, but that number is meaningless here because 79023's axis is reversed, and the vertex convention returns no chord because 79023 starts on the vertex. The pairing that would be worth pricing is 80055 (detached 26.7 cm) against the cluster-19 blob (detached 27.9 cm) -- two detached EM blobs on opposite sides of the star -- but the display prices whole showers, not sub-pieces of one, so I could not compute it and I propose no stored pairing.

[agent-bulk] This event has no EM shower above 20 MeV; the entry that puts it in the numucc_em bucket (em_max 124.3 MeV = shower 46017) is a proton. Verdict is on 46017, the leading pdg-11 shower: NOT an EM shower. It is two segments -- a 1.2 cm pdg 11 stub (the seed) and 51022, a 13.7 cm pdg 2212 track absorbed by pass4_angle at 9.5 cm / 12.0 deg. On shw46017-az-055-el+20 the member set is a single narrow straight line with a tight cloud, no cone, no branching, no widening; rotated to az+085 it is seen near end-on as a compact dense blob about 7 x 3 cm, which is what a stopping proton looks like, not a 124 MeV electron (which would be 30+ cm long and several cm wide). The reconstruction's own PID agrees for 92% of the length (pdg 2212 on 51022); only the 1.2 cm seed is pdg 11. This is a PID statement; on clustering alone the two segments are contiguous and I see nothing to add or remove. Two other in-scope entries are also not EM: 18005 (394.9 MeV, pdg 13) is the 171.9 cm muon -- three cluster-18 segments in a dead straight line within 1.5 deg, visible on both vertex cameras running from the star to the top of the frame, and it is in scope only because the scope rule is on kine_best and not on PID; 50021 (108.3 MeV, pdg 2212) is a lone 9.0 cm proton at 65-74 cm. Vertex judged first and cleared: on vtx-az-055 and vtx-az+065 the muon 18005 starts on the star and the 16.6 cm pdg 2212 segment 18007 (correctly left unowned) is the second prong on it. Scope: 3 of 17 showers in scope (18005, 46017, 50021); the other 14 (18024 7.1 MeV, then 24008 3.1 down to 43014 0.3 MeV) are all under 8 MeV, skipped by the 20 MeV rule, and I did not look at them. Pi0: no reco pi0 group, no gamma slots were assignable, and with no EM object in the event there is no pairing to propose.

[agent-bulk] Leading EM shower 30022 (417.9 MeV, 27 seg): correct. It is detached 12 cm from the vertex, and its 27 members form one cone in one direction -- the angular spread falls with distance exactly as a shower's should (up to 27.7 deg out at 30-40 cm, then <=13.6 deg beyond 80 cm), with the body continuous from the X to about 83 cm. The decisive check is its acceptance plot: 27 orange squares and ZERO blue circles, i.e. there is not a single non-member anywhere in this shower's angle/distance neighbourhood, so nothing is left grey inside the cone and it cannot be under-clustered. Two azimuths (az-055, az+085) show one apex at the X, no kink and no second direction. The one thing I would flag rather than call: the tail. After a continuous body to 83.5 cm there are two isolated fragments at 102.0 cm (112049, 0.8 cm) and 121.7 cm (111048, 0.6 cm pdg 2212), both tier 2 pass4_angle, each behind a ~19 cm gap. On a 418 MeV shower (83 cm is ~6 X0) I read them as tail, not as over-clustering, but they are the same construction that made me record evt280972 as unclear, and they are worth an owner's eye if that tail behaviour is what the round is about. Not marked. Vertex judged first and cleared: cluster 26 gives four prongs all starting on the star -- the 152.9 cm muon 26000 and the 10.2 cm pion 26002 (both correctly left unowned), the 21.4 cm pion 26001 and the 10.5 cm 26003 -- and they converge on it in both the vertex camera and the +-70 cm shower frame. NOT EM, for the record: shower 26001 (61.6 MeV) is reco pdg 211, i.e. the pion track, and it has absorbed three sub-centimetre pdg 13 stubs at 24.8/35.4/42.3 cm along its own extension by pass3_cone; shower 26003 (33.5 MeV) is a single 10.5 cm segment sitting on the vertex in the muon's own cluster. Neither is an EM shower in my reading, but both are inside the 20 MeV scope rule; I make no PID verdict on them because the verdict slot belongs to 30022. Scope: 3 of 6 showers in scope (30022, 26001, 26003); skipped were 78025 (18.5 MeV, pdg 2212, 2.4 cm -- just under the cut), 110047 (6.7 MeV) and 31024 (2.6 MeV), and I did not look at them. Pi0: no reco pi0 group. The capture's automatic slots priced 30022+26003 at 256.1 MeV on the axis convention (theta 139.2 deg) and the kine_pio_ BDT feature says 253.1 MeV at 129.7 deg; that is a back-to-back pair, and 26003 sits on the vertex so it is not a converted photon. 30022 is the only detached photon-like object in the event and has no partner. No pairing proposed.

[agent-bulk] Leading EM shower 19032 (436.7 MeV, 26 seg): correct. On shw19032-az+085 it is a textbook shower -- one apex at the X, a Y-shaped fan opening along one direction, dense cloud, and the yellow member set covers all of it; az-055 shows the same body with no second apex and no kink. Its acceptance plot has 26 member squares and only two blue circles, 56052 (0.8 cm, 29.4 cm out, 23.3 deg) and 62076 (0.3 cm, 72.6 cm, 9.3 deg), each a sub-centimetre object with its own shower id and negligible charge -- so essentially nothing contiguous is left unclaimed inside the cone. The one soft spot, same construction as evt317939 and evt280972: the two outermost members, 65079 (0.8 cm at 83.2 cm, 23.1 deg) and 66080 (1.4 cm at 105.7 cm, 21.3 deg), are tier '-' (outside every pass-1 tier, taken by pass4_angle) and sit at LARGER angle than the members at 60-64 cm, so the cone widens again in the tail instead of narrowing. On 1-2 cm of segment out of a 436 MeV shower I do not call that over-clustering. Not marked. WORTH THE OWNER'S EYE -- the pi0 number: this is the only event in my shard where the display's own pairing lands in the accept window. The automatic slots price 19032+12092 at 175.7 MeV on the axis convention, flagged '[in the code's accept window]', while the kine_pio_ BDT feature says 219.0 MeV and does not close with its own formula (161.1). I do not believe the pair. Gamma2 (shower 12092, 228.8 MeV) starts ON the vertex and on shw12092-az-055 it is a straight narrow 39.4 cm track, one of three straight prongs leaving the star in cluster 12 alongside the 39.9 cm pdg 2212 segment 12088 and the 58.3 cm pdg 13 segment 12091 (both correctly left unowned). A vertex-attached straight track is not a converted photon, so the mass that falls in the window is, in my reading, an accident. 12092 also carries a long thin tail: its 11 members total only 54.8 cm of segment but span 0-148.1 cm, the far ones being 0.2-2.7 cm stubs at 82/97/99/106/120/148 cm taken by pass4_angle at 6-21 deg -- that reads as over-clustering of a track, but the verdict slot belongs to 19032 so it is recorded here in prose, unmarked. Vertex judged first and cleared: three prongs converge on the star in both the vertex camera and the +-94 cm frame. Note for the record that 19032's nearest member is 100 cm from the vertex, which is a long way for a converted photon (about 5 conversion lengths); the vertex is nevertheless well defined by its own three prongs, so I did not call vertex-bad. Scope: 2 of 13 showers in scope (19032, 12092); the other eleven (56052 3.7 MeV down to 64078 0.9 MeV) are all under 4 MeV, skipped by the 20 MeV rule, not examined. No reco pi0 group; no pairing stored.

[agent-bulk] Leading EM shower 6009 (295.7 MeV, 21 seg): correct. On both shower azimuths (az-055, az+085) it is one cone with a single apex at the X, a cluster-6 body of about 49 cm of segment covering the dense cloud out to ~27 cm, then a trail of small on-axis fragments; no kink, no second apex, no straight MIP stem swallowed. Its acceptance plot is 21 member squares and a single blue circle -- 53034, a 0.6 cm object at 64.2 cm / 25.4 deg with its own shower id -- so there is essentially nothing left unclaimed anywhere in its cone and it cannot be under-clustered. It is detached 26 cm from the vertex, i.e. photon-like. Same soft spot as evt317939 and evt349549 and I am flagging it the same way rather than calling it: after the body the member list is ten sub-centimetre-to-2.6 cm stubs taken by pass4_angle out to 79.0 cm (56037, 57038, 40021 which has length 0.0, 38019, 41022, 39020), several of them pdg 13 or 2212, and on the pictures they are isolated dots well clear of the shower body. That trailing-fragment pattern is the single most repeated thing I saw across this shard; not marked. Vertex judged first and cleared: the star carries the 15.5 cm and 3.2 cm pdg 2212 segments 83050 and 83053, both correctly left unowned, and nothing else reaches it. AN 'other_em' RESULT, same as pilot evt284200: there is exactly ONE EM object in this event. Shower 84048 (69.0 MeV) is reco pdg 13, a straight 16.4 cm track detached 12.4 cm from the vertex plus a 1.4 cm pdg 2212 stub; shower 33014 (46.4 MeV) is a single 0.68 cm pdg 2212 fragment 100 cm out whose energy comes from the shower conversion of 22.7 MeV of charge and should not be read as an EM shower. So the reason this event has no pi0 is not a pairing failure -- there is no second photon in the reconstruction. Note the kine_pio_ BDT feature is junk here: it reports mass 46.8 MeV from E1 295.7 (6009) and E2 7.2 (shower 52033, a 1.6 cm fragment) at 60.7 deg, i.e. it paired the shower with a 7 MeV stub. No gamma slots were auto-assigned, no pairing proposed. Scope: 3 of 16 showers in scope (6009, 84048, 33014); the other 13 (50031 9.0 MeV down to 48029 0.2 MeV) are all under 10 MeV, skipped by the 20 MeV rule, and I did not look at them.

[agent-bulk] Leading and only EM shower 18014 (118.6 MeV, 4 seg): correct. Simple event -- a 46.2 cm pdg 13 track (segment 7002, correctly left unowned) leaving the vertex, and this shower detached 10.3 cm from the star on the other side of it. Its four members (18014 9.1 cm, 18013 4.7 cm, 36018 2.1 cm, 35017 1.4 cm) all lie within 9.1 deg of one axis over 0-38.2 cm, and on both shower azimuths (az-055, az+085) the yellow set covers the whole compact blob with one apex at the X and the axis pointing away from the vertex, which is what a converted photon looks like. Nothing is missing: EVERY non-member in the event is at 43 deg or more from its axis (nearest in angle is 16004 at 43.4 deg and 222 cm away), so there is no contiguous unclaimed charge inside the cone -- the same argument as pilot evt284791, and it does not depend on any width measurement. The two outermost members, 36018 (2.1 cm pdg 13 at 21.1 cm) and 35017 (1.4 cm at 38.2 cm), are isolated stubs on the axis rather than part of a continuous body -- the trailing-fragment pattern again, but only two of them and both inside 9.1 deg, so I do not call it. Vertex judged first and cleared with a caveat: only ONE object touches the star, the 46.2 cm track, so the vertex here is simply that track's end point; nothing contradicts it, but there is also nothing to corroborate it, and if the track's direction is the wrong way round the vertex would be at its far end instead. I did not call vertex-bad because there is no visible convergence that disagrees with the star. Scope: 1 of 7 showers in scope (18014); the six skipped are 7003 (8.7 MeV), 7001 (6.3), 26015 (2.3), 16004 (2.0), 27016 (1.1), 17005 (0.5) -- all under 9 MeV, and I did not look at them. Note 7001 and 7003 (2.4 and 3.1 cm, both pdg 11) sit at 45.8 cm from the vertex at the far end of the muon track and read as its end-point fragments. Pi0: no reco pi0 group, no gamma slots auto-assigned, and with a single EM object above 20 MeV there is no second photon to pair -- another 'partner absent' case rather than a mis-pairing.

[agent-bulk] The vertex sits in the middle of a long straight through-going track, so I record this as a vertex result and not as a clustering failure. On vtx-az+065-el+20 there is ONE thin, uniform, dead-straight charge track running corner to corner across the +-101 cm frame -- well over 200 cm long -- and the blue star sits ON it with charge continuing both ways past it; the only structure on the line is a couple of small dense knots that read as delta rays. On vtx-az-055-el+20 the same line shows about 54 cm of dense charge on each side of the star. Nothing converges at the star: no second prong, no stem, no V. Shower 16000 (103.9 MeV, the only shower in scope) is a 20.2 cm slice of that line starting at the star, and on shw16000-az+085-el+20 its yellow member set lies along the track, not across it. So my reading is that the star is a point on a cosmic-like through-going muon and that 16000 is a piece of it, i.e. NOT an EM shower. THE ALTERNATIVE READING, which I cannot rule out: the vertex is right, 16000 is a genuine 100 MeV electron leaving it, and the charge on the other side is a coincident track that happens to be collinear -- the display's cloud line says '2 of 13 clusters carry the reconstruction (ids 11, 16)', and cluster 11 contributes NO segments at all to this dump, so I cannot check whether the far half of the line is the same object as the near half. That is why the verdict is the undecidable bucket. WHAT I FOUND BEFORE I SAW THE WIDE FRAMES, recorded because it is checkable either way: on shower 16000's acceptance plot there are 3 member squares and 4 blue circles, and all four circles are INSIDE the pass-1 gate box -- 46008 (1.4 cm at 26.6 cm / 3.3 deg), 47009 (0.4 cm at 32.1 cm / 5.2 deg), 41007 (0.6 cm at 34.2 cm / 4.4 deg) and 36002 (0.4 cm pdg 2212 at 69.4 cm / 5.3 deg), every one tier 1 -- while the two non-seed members it DID take, 39005 (60.3 cm / 3.6 deg) and 40006 (66.7 cm / 5.3 deg), are farther away at the same angle. Read on its own that is a clean under-clustering signature. I deliberately did NOT record marks for it: under the through-going-track reading those fragments are pieces of the muon and growing the shower onto them would be the wrong correction, so the two readings disagree about what the fix is and I am not going to pick. Scope: 1 of 8 showers in scope (16000); the seven skipped are 46008 7.7 MeV, 41007 5.5, 38004 3.0, 36002 2.2, 47009 2.1, 35001 0.3, 37003 0.2 -- all under 8 MeV; note that four of them are exactly the fragments discussed above. Pi0: no reco pi0 group, no gamma slots assignable, nothing to pair.
